subject: Aperture renewal — usage health, uptick readiness, and commit options
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@apertureanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aperture Analytics Procurement <procurement@apertureanalytics.com>, Elena Vega <elena.vega@apertureanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aperture renewal review — Q4 usage and potential commit uplift

Hi Soojin,

Hope you had a good holiday. Our renewal window for Aperture is coming up in March and procurement asked me to get a clear read on our consumption trends, costs, and options for increasing committed capacity. High-level asks: 1) Q4 token spend broken down by workspace and feature (generation vs embeddings), 2) performance notes (latency/throughput) for our top models, and 3) a few viable commit/term options with economics so we can model ROI.

Elena (cc) will coordinate PO timing. I'm attaching a short procurement intent doc on our side (procurement_intent.pdf). Can you share a short readout and a 30–45 minute time slot next week to review? We prefer mornings PST.

Thanks,
Sam
Senior ML Engineer
Aperture Analytics

Attachment: procurement_intent.pdf (attachment)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@apertureanalytics.com>
Cc: Aperture Analytics Procurement <procurement@apertureanalytics.com>, Elena Vega <elena.vega@apertureanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal review — Q4 usage and potential commit uplift

Hi Sam — thanks for the note and the procurement doc. We're available to run a tight renewal health check and outline commit tiers you can model. Attached is an initial usage pack (aperture_q4_usage_breakdown.csv) and a quick cost split (aperture_cost_breakdown.xlsx). Top-line observations from Q4:

- Total token spend: ~1.9B tokens (up 38% QoQ).
- Generation vs embeddings: ~65% generation, 35% embeddings; embeddings cost per 1M tokens ~30% lower due to batching.
- Top model: redwood-g6-xl for generation (median p95 latency 110ms on hosted tier); embeddings on redwood-embed-2 (mean latency 45ms).
- Spike behavior: three high-traffic windows correlated with customer batch jobs (we recommend prefix caching to cut marginal cost during jobs).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-minute sync next Tue/Wed morning PST — I'll include Ben from Commercial to walk pricing tiers.
2) We'll prepare 3 commit scenarios (12-mo standard, 12-mo with 3-mo canary, 24-mo discount path) with per-token economics and burst credit allowances.
3) Include a short perf delta note if you considered Dedicated.

Available slots: Tue 9:00–11:00, Wed 10:00–11:30 PST. Which works?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: aperture_q4_usage_breakdown.csv, aperture_cost_breakdown.xlsx

Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal review — pricing options + uplift scenarios

Hi Sam and team — looping in a few numbers you can drop into your internal model. Short version: increasing committed capacity reduces unit cost and unlocks burst credits; below are three practical paths we recommend based on your Q4 run-rate.

Scenario A — Conservative (12-mo)
- Commit: +25% over current run-rate
- Effective unit price: $0.95 / 1k tokens (hosted)
- Burst credits: 15% monthly
- Typical ROI: pays back within 6–9 months for steady growth customers

Scenario B — Accelerate (12-mo with 3-mo canary)
- Commit: +50%
- Effective unit price: $0.78 / 1k tokens
- Burst credits: 30% monthly, priority routing during bursts
- Includes upgrade path to Dedicated with 30–45 day notice (no migration downtime)

Scenario C — Long-term (24-mo)
- Commit: +75%
- Effective unit price: $0.62 / 1k tokens
- Burst credits: 40% monthly
- Includes a one-time migration advisory credit and extended SLAs

Notes: We can also model a hybrid for you (part hosted, part dedicated) if you want guaranteed latency on critical endpoints while keeping non-critical jobs on hosted. Attached is a PDF with the formal uplift options and a sample ROI grid.

If the team agrees, we can prepare a redline-friendly amendment (DocuSign link in the follow-up) and schedule a kickoff with CS to scope migration or canary windows.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_uptick_options-v2.pdf
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@apertureanalytics.com>

Cc: Aperture Analytics Procurement <procurement@apertureanalytics.com>, Elena Vega <elena.vega@apertureanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal review — pricing options + uplift scenarios

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear tiers. A few follow-ups from our side before we take this to procurement: 

1) Performance: can you confirm p95 latencies for embeddings and generation if we move 30% of traffic to a Dedicated pool? We need conservative estimates for SLA comparisons.
2) Retention/compliance: procurement asked whether logs/audit trails for inference calls are accessible for 365 days and whether we can push retention to a private S3 (we have SOC2 requirements).
3) PO timing: if we pick Scenario B, what is the earliest start date and how do burst credits apply during the first billing period?

Also forwarding procurement_intent.pdf and a short internal compliance checklist.

Sam

Subject: Re: Aperture renewal review — pricing options + uplift scenarios

Hi Sam and Elena — following up with the operational clarifications you asked for and recommended next steps. Short answers first:

- Dedicated perf: moving ~30% of steady traffic to a Dedicated pool (N1-equivalent) should yield p95 generation latency ~55–70ms and embeddings p95 ~25–35ms depending on sequence length. We'll provide a runbook with benchmarked numbers for your specific models in the next 48 hours.
- Retention: audit logs are available for 365 days; we can export to your S3 bucket via a signed transfer; KMS integration supported for encryption-at-rest.
- Start date / burst credits: Scenario B can start as soon as a signed amendment is in place; first billing period includes prorated burst credits (applies proportionally to committed capacity for that month).

Proposed execution path:
1) Sign a 3-month canary addendum to the renewal (reduces upfront risk while preserving pricing in Scenario B).
2) CS runbook + perf bench (Marcus) delivered within 48 hours after addendum signature.
3) Procurement to issue PO on signature; we provision Dedicated nodes within 7–10 business days after PO and onboarding begins.

Action items:
- Soojin: send the canary addendum draft to Aperture and DocuSign link.
- Ben: prepare final pricing sheet with prorated start examples.
- Sam/Elena: confirm preferred start date and a PO owner.

I'll standby to jump on a call if you want to triage any of the technical details.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
